messages.content: What's the population in New York right now?

function.name: time_converter
function.description: Converts the local time of user's region to the target region's local time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_timezone.description: The timezone of the user in string format. Example: 'Pacific Time (US & Canada)'

target_timezone.description: The target timezone in string format where user wants to know the local time. Example: 'Eastern Time (US & Canada)'

time.description: The local time of user's timezone in string format (24 hr format). Optional parameter. Example: '15:30:00'

message.content:
I don’t have access to live databases, but I can give you the most recent official figures:

| City | Population Estimate |
|------|---------------------|
| **New York City** | ~8.9 million (U.S. Census Bureau, 2022‑23 American Community Survey) |

If you’re looking at the entire state of New York, it’s roughly 19–20 million people as of the same period.

These numbers come from U.S. Census estimates released annually. For the absolute latest count—especially if there has been significant migration since then—you’d want to check the U.S. Census Bureau’s “Population Estimates Program” website or the NYC Department of Health’s demographic reports.
message.reasoning:
The user asks about current population in New York. This requires up-to-date data; we don't have real-time info. We can provide approximate estimate based on latest census or estimates. Provide context and note it's an approximation.

We should not use tool because no conversion needed. Just answer with best available knowledge.
